g.title: frag_micro_nn_distance → frag_meso_contact_component_count upward 局部最近邻间距改变鱼之间形成接触边的概率：当许多鱼彼此远离时，原生接触图更易断开，从而增加连通分量数；该关系依赖空间排布而非由定义直接决定。
frag_micro_nn_distance → frag_macro_largest_component_fraction upward 个体局部间距增大会削弱跨邻域接触链，使最大连通分量占比可能下降；但若存在少数稠密核心，影响可被缓冲，因此不是确定性聚合。
frag_meso_contact_component_count → frag_macro_largest_component_fraction upward 鱼群分裂为更多连通分量时，最大分量占比通常可能降低；但多分量可包含一个主导核心，故这是动态结构候选而非代数恒等。
elong_micro_axis_alignment → elong_macro_global_eigen_ratio upward 大量个体沿群体主轴对齐时，定向游动可能累积为整体位置分布的各向异性拉伸；个体转向上限和随机扰动使对齐不必然转化为等比例全局拉伸。

g.title: elong_macro_global_eigen_ratio → frag_meso_contact_component_count downward Global elongation along a principal axis can separate fish that were previously in contact, especially across the stretched direction, thereby breaking native contact links and increasing the number of contact-graph components. The effect is dynamic and not definitional because elongation does not determine which contacts persist.

g.title: frag_meso_contact_component_count → frag_micro_nn_distance downward When the fish contact graph splits into more components, individual fish are less likely to be held within a dense common neighborhood; this can allow local nearest-neighbor spacing to increase as fish adjust to sparse or disconnected local groups. The relation is probabilistic because contact components and metric nearest-neighbor distances are not the same representation.

g.title: frag_macro_largest_component_fraction → frag_micro_nn_distance downward A declining largest-component fraction means the school is increasingly concentrated in smaller components or isolated groups; fish outside the dominant connected cluster experience weaker collective spacing constraints and can exhibit larger nearest-neighbor gaps. This is a plausible macro-to-micro dynamic effect rather than a direct definition, since nearest-neighbor distance is measured independently of graph membership.

g.title: frag_micro_nn_distance → elong_micro_axis_alignment intra_scale A fish with larger nearest-neighbor spacing has weaker local social constraint from nearby schoolmates; over subsequent steps its heading may be less entrained by the group's principal axis, so its absolute axis alignment can change. This is a dynamic micro-level candidate effect rather than a definitional aggregation.

g.title: elong_macro_global_eigen_ratio → frag_macro_largest_component_fraction intra_scale Greater global position elongation spreads fish along a major axis and can push some pairwise distances beyond contact range, which may reduce the fraction of fish remaining in the largest contact component. The candidate effect is mediated by contact formation and is not a definitional identity between the two macro indicators.

g.title: N1 | frag_micro_nn_distance Focal fish nearest-neighbor distance Scale: micro | Phenomenon: school_fragmentation Definition: For run r and step t, let V_t={i: role_i(t)='fish'}. For i in V_t, d_i(t)=min_{j in V_t, j!=i} sqrt((x_i(t)-x_j(t))^2+(y_i(t)-y_j(t))^2). If |V_t|<2, d_i(t)=NaN. N2 | frag_meso_contact_component_count Fish contact-graph component count Scale: meso | Phenomenon: school_fragmentation Definition: At (r,t), build G_t=(V_t,E_t) with V_t={i: role_i(t)='fish'} and E_t={{i,j}: i,j in V_t, i!=j, and (agent_id=i, partner_id=j) or (agent_id=j, partner_id=i) appears in contacts at (r,t)}. Let C_1(t),...,C_{K(t)}(t) be the connected components of G_t. K(t)=number of components. N4 | elong_micro_axis_alignment Focal fish heading alignment with group principal axis Scale: micro | Phenomenon: school_elongation Definition: For run r and step t, let V_t={i: role_i(t)='fish'}. Let mu(t)=(1/|V_t|) sum_{j in V_t} p_j(t) and Sigma(t)=(1/(|V_t|-1)) sum_{j in V_t} (p_j(t)-mu(t))(p_j(t)-mu(t))^T with p_j=(x_j,y_j). Let lambda1>=lambda2 be eigenvalues of Sigma(t) and u1(t) a unit eigenvector for lambda1. For i in V_t, h_i(t)=(cos heading_i(t), sin heading_i(t)); a_i(t)=|h_i(t) dot u1(t)|. If |V_t|<3 or lambda1=lambda2, set a_i(t)=NaN. Execution: {'2a815b4dfe4f47b8ac2416fac04456e5': {'status': 'success', 'series_file': 'indicator_series/2a815b4dfe4f47b8ac2416fac04456e5/elong_micro_axis_alignment.parquet', 'series_sha256': '42ac8d51aeba9ef44e2d72ab20454b4af12dac3ef6056aec2a23c1cfd979cdcc'}}

N6 | elong_macro_global_eigen_ratio Global fish position eigenvalue ratio Scale: macro | Phenomenon: school_elongation Definition: For V_t={i: role_i(t)='fish'} at (r,t), let mu(t)=(1/|V_t|) sum_{j in V_t} p_j(t) and Sigma(t)=(1/(|V_t|-1)) sum_{j in V_t} (p_j(t)-mu(t))(p_j(t)-mu(t))^T. Let lambda1(t)>=lambda2(t)>=0 be eigenvalues of Sigma(t). R(t)=lambda1(t)/lambda2(t) if lambda2(t)>0; NaN if lambda2(t)=0 or |V_t|<3.
